{{2022–23 Southeastern Conference men's basketball standings}}
The '''2022–23 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team''' represented [[Auburn University]] during the [[2022–23 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]] as a member of the [[Southeastern Conference]]. The team's head coach was [[Bruce Pearl]] in his ninth season at Auburn.  The team played their home games at [[Neville Arena]] in [[Auburn, Alabama]]. They finished the season 20–11, 10–8 in SEC play to finish in seventh. As the No. 7 seed, they were defeated by No. 10 seed [[2022–23 Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball team|Arkansas]] in the second round. They received an at-large bid to the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 9 seed in the Midwest Region, where they defeated [[2022–23 Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball team|Iowa]] in the First round before falling to [[2022–23 Houston Cougars men's basketball team|Houston]] in the Second round.

==Previous season==
The [[2021–22 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team]] finished the [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2021–22 season]] 28–6, 15–3 in SEC play to finish as regular season champions. As the No. 1 seed, they were defeated by No. 8 seed [[2021–22 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team|Texas A&M]] in the quarterfinals. They received an at-large bid to the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 2 seed in the Midwest Region, where they defeated [[2021–22 Jacksonville State Gamecocks men's basketball team|Jacksonville State]] in the First round before being upset by [[2021–22 Miami Hurricanes men's basketball team|Miami]] in the Second round.

On January 24, 2022, the team was voted first in the [[AP Poll#Men's basketball|AP poll]] for the first time in program history, in the midst of a nineteen game winning streak.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2022-01-24|title=Auburn No. 1 for first time in history of AP poll|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33139003/auburn-tigers-no-1-first-history-ap-top-25-men-basketball-poll|access-date=2022-02-08|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref>
